newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch firms to buy Bell Lines' Rotterdam terminal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch firms to buy Bell Lines' Rotterdam terminal.

text.p: The Rotterdam port authority said on Thursday a group of Dutch companies had made a business plan to take over the Bell Mertens Terminal in Rotterdam from troubled Irish shipping firm Bell Lines.

Among the members of the Dutch group is Europe Combined Terminals (ECT), in which transport firms Nedlloyd, Pakhoed and Internatio-Mueller own stakes. Other members are a number of unlisted Rotterdam-based firms.
The port authority said the takeover plan was aimed at continuing stevedoring activities at the Bell Mertens Terminal which it said had good prospects.
It added that the chances of a successful takeover seemed fairly good so that the consequences for the Rotterdam port of a possible bankruptcy of Bell Lines could be limited.
The Bell Mertens Terminal started operations about a year ago and handles about 260,000 containers per year. Fewer than half of these are handled for Bell Lines.
Earlier this week a spokesman for the Irish group said the deadline for agreeing restructuring plans for Bell Lines had been extended to July 5.
